decision_label: REAL-MIXTURE ADAPTATION IS VIABLE BUT NO CLEAR PRODUCT GAIN
decision_basis: Primary human blind listening (18 items, one headphone pass, unblinded 2026-09-15; see listening_pack/HUMAN_LISTENING_RESULTS.md) combined with the frozen machine-side record (REAL_TEST_RESULTS.md, GENERALIZATION_RESULTS.md, DEV_RESULTS.md).
adaptation_viability_evidence: Trained on authentic raw mixtures only (no synthetic target+nuisance anywhere): zero collapse and zero raw-passthrough at every DEV eval (REAL_TEST/FAILURE_CASES); DEV cross-context consistency 0.0609 -> 0.0455 (-25%); TEST_GENERALIZATION on 14 unseen recordings: zero collapse (S1W was -27.7 dB), click retention -0.96 dB vs zero-shot -1.20 dB; sealed groups within +-0.2 dB RMS of zero-shot with slightly better transient retention on all six. Human listening heard no deletion, no passthrough, no instability.
catastrophic_target_deletion_evidence: None observed machine-side (worst anchor -1.0 dB vs teacher on a -6 dB guard; click retention better than zero-shot on all sealed groups) and none heard (interaction described as 'very obvious', 'excellent and appears complete', 'slightly better/more natural').
selectivity_evidence: c3 Taiko-prompt positive pattern audibly survives adaptation (item_17 'almost no NPC audible ... similar positive behavior to item_08'); machine-side: equal suppression, transient retention marginally closer to raw on all six sealed groups.
product_gain_evidence: Blinded comparison ZERO-SHOT vs S1R: S1R clearly preferred in 0 of 6 groups (bar was >=3/6); explicit ties in c2 ('same conclusion'), mirror-positive tie in c3, inconclusive tie in c7, tie in c8, at most a faint c6 edge for S1R (interaction naturalness, matching RAW) and an ambiguous c1. No group where S1R is clearly worse.
primary_interpretation: Teacher-only / consistency-dominated adaptation preserves the teacher but adds no audible new information. The student inherited zero-shot's selectivity AND zero-shot's remaining nuisances (neighboring Taiko machines, NPC speech, minor underwater/discontinuity on strong-suppression items). A stable real-domain training substrate now exists; new information is required to move beyond it.

listening_evidence.pack: listening_pack/ frozen fixed-gain pack (18 items, one common per-group gain from RAW, relative levels preserved to 1e-05 dB)
listening_evidence.playback_device: headphones (S1W was speakers) - NO cross-stage timbre claims made; internal S1R comparison valid

why_B_and_not_A: A required audible preference for S1R on >=3/6 groups. The owner could not reliably distinguish S1R from zero-shot in the blinded pack; observed edges are single-group and faint. The machine-side record agrees: +-0.2 dB RMS, equal suppression, small transient-retention refinement only.
why_B_and_not_C: C-class failure modes are all ruled out by ear and by measurement: no deletion of authentic interaction, no raw passthrough, no instability, teacher selectivity preserved. S1R's question ('can CLAPSep be adapted on real mixtures WITHOUT destroying zero-shot selectivity?') is answered YES - it just does not improve the product.
stage_should_not_continue_with: further teacher-only / consistency-dominated distillation of the same frozen teacher

next_stage_recommendation.focus: S2A - reference-conditioned real-mixture extraction: add ALIGNED PRISTINE MUSIC REFERENCE as a genuinely new information source (a native product input), via a minimal near-no-op adapter on the frozen S1R base
explicitly_not_started_yet: complex-mask / phase-capable reconstruction (reserved for a future stage if underwater remains dominant)

explicitly_not_done: No additional model experiment after the verdict
No SI-SDR / recall / suppression claims from listening (no ground truth exists)
No cross-stage S1W<->S1R timbre comparison (different playback devices)
